parameter_edit.default_value_help: Select a default value in case the lookup result is empty
parameter_edit.empty_result: The event definition query is only executed if a value for the parameter is present. If the lookup result is empty, the execution will be skipped and treated as if the <emphasis>Search Query</emphasis> found no messages. If an execution is desired a <emphasis>Default Value</emphasis> that yields the desired search result needs to be provided. For example, (depending on the use case) a wildcard like <inlineCode>{{wildcard}}</inlineCode> can be a meaningful Default Value.
parameter_edit.empty_result_title: Behavior on empty lookup result list
parameter_edit.general_usage: After declaring it, the parameter <inlineCode>{{parameter}}</inlineCode> in your query, will be replaced with the list of results from the lookup table. The list of results will be presented in the form of a Lucene BooleanQuery. E.g.: <inlineCode>{{example}}</inlineCode>

parameter_edit.limitations: Please note, the maximum number of supported results is depending on the <inlineCode>{{setting}}</inlineCode> setting. If the lookup table returns more results, the query will fail in your indexer.

http_doc.lookup_url_text: The URL that will be used for the HTTP request. To use the lookup key in the URL, the ${key} value can be used. This variable will be replaced by the actual key that is passed to a lookup function.
http_doc.single_value_text: This JSONPath expression will be used to parse the single value of the lookup result. (example: $.user.full_name)
http_doc.multi_value_text: This JSONPath expression will be used to parse the multi value of the lookup result. (example: $.users[*]) The multi value JSONPath setting is optional. Without it, the single value is also present in the multi value result.
http_doc.http_useragent_text: This is the <emphasis>User-Agent</emphasis> header that will be used for the HTTP requests. You should include some contact details so owners of the services you query know whom to contact if issues arise. (like excessive API requests from your cluster)
http_doc.intro: The HTTPJSONPath data adapter executes <emphasis>HTTP GET</emphasis> requests to lookup a key and parses the result based on configured JSONPath expressions.
http_doc.two_values: Every lookup table result has two values. A <emphasis>single value</emphasis> and a <emphasis>multi value</emphasis>. The single value will be used when the lookup result is expected to be a string, number or boolean. The multi value will be used when the lookup result is expected to be a map or list.
http_doc.example_intro: This shows an example configuration and the values that will be returned from a lookup.
http_doc.example_url: The configured URL is https://example.com/api/users/${key} and the ${key} gets replaced by jane during the lookup request.

caffeine_doc.cache_size_text: Every cache has a maximum number of entries, unbounded caches are not supported.
caffeine_doc.expire_access_text: The cache will remove entries after a fixed time since they have been used the last time.
caffeine_doc.expire_access_result: This results in the cache behaving as a space limited least recently used cache.
caffeine_doc.expire_write_text: The cache will remove entries after a fixed time since they have been entered into the cache.
caffeine_doc.expire_write_result: This results in entries that are never older than the given time, which can be important for regularly changing data, such as configuration state of external systems.
caffeine_doc.intro: The in-memory cache maintains recently used values from data adapters.
caffeine_doc.heap_hint: Please make sure your {{productName}} servers have enough heap to accommodate the cached entries and monitor the cache efficiency.
caffeine_doc.local_hint: The cache is local to each {{productName}} server, they do not share the entries.
caffeine_doc.example: For example, if you have two servers, they will maintain a completely independent cache from each other.

caffeine_fields.max_size_help: The limit of the number of entries the cache keeps in memory.
caffeine_fields.expire_access_help: If enabled, entries are removed from the cache after the specified time from when they were last used.
caffeine_fields.expire_write_help: If enabled, entries are removed from the cache after the specified time from when they were first used.
caffeine_fields.ignore_null_help: When enabled, empty lookup results will be ignored and not cached.
caffeine_fields.ttl_empty_help: Empty results are removed from the cache after the specified time.
caffeine_fields.must_be_positive: Must be 0 or a positive number

dns_doc.a: Returns both a single_value containing one of the IPv4 addresses that the hostname resolves to, and a multi_value containing all IPv4 addresses that the hostname resolves to. Input for this type must be a pure domain name (eg. api.example.com).
dns_doc.a_aaaa: Returns both a single_value containing one of the IPv4 or IPv6 addresses that the hostname resolves to (will return IPv4 if available), and a multi_value containing all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses that the hostname resolves to. Input for this type must be a pure domain name (eg. api.example.com).
dns_doc.aaaa: Returns both a single_value containing one of the IPv6 addresses that the hostname resolves to, and a multi_value containing all IPv6 addresses that the hostname resolves to. Input for this type must be a pure domain name (eg. api.example.com).
dns_doc.cache_ttl_override: If enabled, the TTL for this adapter's cache will be overridden with the specified value.
dns_doc.ptr: Returns a single_value containing the PTR value if defined for the IP address. The domain field displays the domain name (with no subdomains). The full_domain field displays the full un-trimmed host name/PTR value. The input for this type must be a pure IPv4 or IPv6 address (eg. 10.0.0.1 or 2622:f3b0:4000:812::200c).
dns_doc.request_timeout: The DNS request timeout in milliseconds.
dns_doc.server_ips: A comma-separated list of DNS server IP addresses and optional ports to use (eg. 192.168.1.1:5353, 192.168.1.244). Leave this blank to use the DNS server defined for your local system. All requests use port 53 unless otherwise specified.
dns_doc.txt: Returns a multi_value with all TXT records defined for the hostname. Input for this type must be a pure domain name (eg. api.example.com).
